newsitem.title: USA: Viacom sees '96 cash flow meeting forecasts.
newsitem.headline: Viacom sees '96 cash flow meeting forecasts.

text.p: Viacom Inc executives told a private investors meeting on Tuesday that the entertainment group would meet or exceed cash flow estimates of $2.185 billion for 1996, according to people who attended the meeting.

The executives at the all-day meeting said Viacom was on track to match or better analysts' mean estimate of $2.185 billion for EBITDA, a measure of cash flow defined as earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amoritization.
Officials of Viacom declined to comment on the meeting.
But executives said EBITDA at Blockbuster, Viacom's retailing arm, would likely be slightly below the mean forecast of $803 million from Wall Street analysts.

Bill Fields, Blockbuster's new chairman, told the investors he aimed to return the video and music retailer's EBITDA growth to the 15-20 percent range in coming years, according to people who attended the meeting.
Fields said Blockbuster would continue expanding, aiming to open between 700 and 850 new stores in 1997, while making the existing network of some 5,000 outlets more efficient.

Fields said the company would in early 1997, after the heavy fourth-quarter sales season, review all 500 Blockbuster Music outlets with an eye to shutting as many as 50 based on sales and profitability.
Blockbuster will cut costs by dealing directly with Hollywood studios on purchasing videos, reducing handling and consolidating internal purchasing operations, he said.

Blockbuster will also move to diversify its offerings on an individual store basis by offering new or varied products in a campaign to become a neighborhood entertainment outlet, people who attended the meeting quoted Fields as saying.
Fields also said Blockbuster's vast database of customer information had not been fully exploited and offered growth potential.

Blockbuster was purchased by Viacom in 1994 as part of its long campaign to win control of Paramount Communications, but slowing growth at the group has spurred worries on Wall Street and speculation Viacom might spin off the business.
Shares of Viacom closed up 3/8 at 37-1/8, well below the issue's 52-week high of 50-5/8.
